title: Xbox Series X|S Storage for GTA 6: Expansion Card or USB Drive?
summary: GTA 6 can be stored on USB but must run from internal or expansion storage on Xbox. Here's how I'd make room, with eight cards and drives worth buying.
body_markdown:
Xbox storage is more confusing than it should be, and GTA 6 is going to expose that for a lot of people in November. The short version: GTA 6 is an Xbox Series X|S game, so it has to be played from the console's internal SSD or from a Storage Expansion Card. A USB drive can hold it, but it cannot run it.


That one rule decides most of what you should buy. The game launches on 19 November 2026, and digital pre-orders can pre-load from 12 November, so this is the month to sort it out.


## Step One: Check How Much Space You Really Have


The Series X ships with a 1TB SSD, of which roughly 802GB is usable for games. The original Series S has a 512GB SSD with about 364GB usable, and there is also a 1TB Series S. Rockstar has not announced GTA 6's install size, but modern open-world games are large, and on a 512GB Series S I would assume you will need to clear space or add some.


Open Settings, then System, then Storage devices. It shows you exactly what is on each drive.


## Step Two: Decide What Has to Stay Fast


Any game built for Series X|S, GTA 6 included, has to sit on fast storage to be played. Xbox One and older backward-compatible games can run straight from a USB drive. So the cheapest plan is often to move your Xbox One-era games to USB and keep the internal SSD for new releases.


## Step Three: Add Fast Storage With an Expansion Card


The Storage Expansion Card plugs into the slot on the back of the console. It is a proprietary format, so a normal M.2 SSD will not work here. Only licensed cards do. Once inserted, it behaves like the internal drive, Quick Resume included.


The[SanDisk Optimus GX C50 2TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820173749?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) is the one I would buy. It is officially licensed, the listing says it matches the console's SSD performance, and 2TB is more than double the space a Series X gives you for games out of the box. If you only need breathing room, the[SanDisk Optimus GX C50 1TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820173750?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) is the same card at half the capacity.


Seagate made the original expansion cards, and they are still the reference. The[Seagate Storage Expansion Card 2TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIC8D2M6S4316?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) and the[Seagate Storage Expansion Card 1TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIC8D2M6S4317?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) work with both Series X and Series S. Between SanDisk and Seagate at the same capacity, I would buy whichever is available. They do the same job.


## Step Four: Add Cheap Space for Everything Else


A USB drive is where your back catalogue lives. Here the choice is between a hard drive for capacity and an SSD for faster transfers.


The[WD_BLACK P10 6TB Game Drive for Xbox](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16822234571?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) is a portable hard drive on USB 3.2 Gen 1, with speeds listed up to 130MB/s. WD says it holds up to 150 games. The[Seagate Game Drive for Xbox 5TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/1E8-004Z-00558?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) is the equivalent from Seagate, also on USB 3.2 Gen 1.


If you shuffle games back and forth often, an SSD saves a lot of waiting. The[WD_BLACK D30 Game Drive SSD for Xbox, 1TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIBTK0KVJ9615?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) uses USB 3.2 Gen 2 and lists speeds up to 900MB/s. WD's own wording is clear about the limits: play and store Xbox One games, archive Series X|S games. If you also want a drive for a PC or laptop, the[Samsung T9 2TB portable SSD](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820147881?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) does the same storage job and is rated up to 2,000MB/s on a USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 port.


## My Setup Advice


Series S with 512GB: add a 1TB expansion card and move older games to a USB drive. Series X with a crowded drive: a 2TB expansion card is the cleanest fix. Big back catalogue: a WD P10 or Seagate Game Drive for storage. Do the shuffle before 12 November and the pre-load will have room. More options are in Newegg's[Xbox storage expansion card listings](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=xbox+series+x+storage+expansion+card&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_xbox-series-storage-gta-6) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can I play GTA 6 from an external USB drive on Xbox?** No. Games built for Xbox Series X|S must run from the internal SSD or a Storage Expansion Card. You can store them on USB and move them back to play.


**Can I use a regular M.2 SSD in my Xbox Series X?** No. The expansion slot uses a proprietary card format, so you need a licensed Storage Expansion Card such as the Seagate or SanDisk models.


**How much usable storage does an Xbox Series S have?** The original 512GB Series S has about 364GB available for games. The Series X's 1TB drive has about 802GB available.


**How big is GTA 6 on Xbox?** Rockstar has not published the install size yet. Pre-loading for digital pre-orders starts on 12 November 2026.


**Is a USB SSD worth it over a hard drive?** For moving games between drives, yes, it is much quicker. For simply storing a large back catalogue, a hard drive gives you more space for the money.
